past_medical_history: Autoimmune thyroiditis (Graves disease treated with radioiodine 2 years ago, now hypothyroid on levothyroxine)

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented. Normal cognition and language.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Left ptosis — levator excursion 4mm. Complete fatigable ptosis left eye on sustained upgaze at 35 seconds. Right ptosis mild intermittent. Esotropia left eye at rest (left medial rectus/adductor weakness causing false impression of esotropia — actually left lateral rectus weakness). Vertical diplopia on upgaze. Pupils equal, reactive. Bilateral mild facial weakness — patient unable to close eyes tightly against resistance. No proptosis.
neurological_exam.motor: Shoulder abductors 4/5 bilaterally. Hip flexors 4+/5. Neck flexors 4-/5. Distal strength 5/5. Fatigability: neck flexion fails after 30 seconds sustained effort.
neurological_exam.gait: Normal. Mildly waddling after walking one block.
neurological_exam.additional: Nasal voice quality after sustained speech. Difficulty chewing — jaw fatigues after 2-3 minutes eating. NIF -61 cmH2O (normal). No respiratory distress.

patient.chief_complaint: Left eyelid drooping with double vision and jaw fatigue for 8 weeks
patient.history_present_illness: A 29-year-old woman with a history of Graves disease treated with radioiodine (now hypothyroid on levothyroxine) presented with 8 weeks of left eyelid drooping, double vision, and jaw fatigue. She first noticed her left eyelid drooping while studying late at night approximately 8 weeks ago. Initially she thought it was related to sleep deprivation from graduate school deadlines. However, the ptosis persisted during the day and worsened in the afternoon. She started experiencing double vision approximately 6 weeks ago — she described seeing two images side by side when looking to the right, and vertical separation of images when looking up. She noticed that her jaw became very fatigued when eating — by the third or fourth bite of a tough food she needed to rest her jaw for 30 seconds before continuing. Her speech became noticeably nasal after she had been speaking for more than a few minutes. She denied any difficulty swallowing liquids or solids but acknowledged food 'sometimes takes longer to chew.' She has had no headache, no limb numbness or tingling, no falls, no bowel or bladder symptoms. She initially saw a student health clinic who attributed the ptosis to allergic conjunctivitis and treated her with antihistamine eye drops without improvement. She subsequently saw an ophthalmologist who ruled out structural eyelid pathology and confirmed no proptosis — noting her prior Graves disease history, the ophthalmologist was concerned about reactivation of thyroid eye disease. However, thyroid function tests performed 2 weeks ago were normal (TSH 2.2). She was then referred to neurology. Her family history includes thyroid disease and she had a recent flare of anxiety attributed to her graduate school stress, for which she declined medication.

findings.significance: Clearly abnormal — facial muscle NMJ involvement confirmed

findings.result: Complete resolution of left ptosis and esotropia within 45 seconds of IV edrophonium 10mg

specialized_test.impression: Clearly abnormal RNS with 15-24% decremental responses. Masseter RNS (24%) is the most abnormal muscle — consistent with the prominent jaw fatigue symptom. Dramatically positive tensilon test. Diagnosis of myasthenia gravis is unequivocal.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Anti-AChR Binding 8.7 nmol/L (H), Anti-AChR Blocking 62% % (H), Anti-AChR Modulating 78% % (H).
abnormal_values_summary: TRAb negative (Graves inactive — thyroid eye disease excluded)

findings.description: Thymic tissue with fatty involution appropriate for age 29. No discrete mass. No thymoma identified.

ct.impression: CT chest: No thymoma. Thymus shows mild residual thymic tissue appropriate for age. In a 29-year-old woman with AChR-positive generalized MG without thymoma, thymectomy is still recommended (MGTX trial evidence for patients <65 with generalized MG).
recommended_actions: Thymectomy still recommended per MGTX trial even without thymoma
Focus on immunosuppression and symptom management

output.impression: Severely abnormal SFEMG confirming MG. Consistent with markedly elevated AChR antibodies. Not required for diagnosis but confirms severity.

findings.description: No anterior mediastinal mass on repeat contrast-enhanced CT. Residual thymic tissue only.

output.impression: No thymoma confirmed on contrast-enhanced CT. Thymectomy still indicated per MGTX trial (Class I evidence). Patient age 29 — well within recommended age range for benefit from thymectomy in generalized MG.

abnormal_values_summary: Anti-TPO 62 (elevated but not active Graves — TRAb negative)
TED excluded — ptosis from MG, not thyroid eye disease

output.proposed: Pyridostigmine 60mg q4-6h AND prednisone 15mg daily AND azathioprine 50mg titrating to 2-3mg/kg for MG in patient on levothyroxine
interactions: Prednisone + levothyroxine: corticosteroids may reduce levothyroxine absorption — separate dosing by 2 hours
contraindications: Mycophenolate contraindicated — woman of reproductive age (teratogenic)
warnings: Levothyroxine absorption can be reduced by corticosteroids — advise taking levothyroxine 30-60 minutes before meals and 2h before prednisone
Monitor CBC monthly for first 3 months on azathioprine
alternatives: Azathioprine preferred over mycophenolate in this reproductive-age patient

output.query: MGTX trial thymectomy nonthymomatous myasthenia gravis evidence

results.title: Randomized Trial of Thymectomy in Myasthenia Gravis (MGTX)
results.finding: Thymectomy + prednisone superior to prednisone alone at 3 years in patients aged 18-65 with generalized AChR-positive MG; lower time-weighted average QMG score, less alternate-day prednisone, fewer hospitalizations, higher complete stable remission rate

results.title: MGTX 5-year follow-up
results.finding: Benefit of thymectomy over prednisone alone persisted at 5 years; 67% reduction in prednisone requirement; thymectomy recommended for all patients 18-65 with generalized AChR-positive MG regardless of CT chest findings

output.summary: MGTX trial (NEJM 2016, 5-year follow-up 2022) provides Class I evidence that thymectomy + prednisone is superior to prednisone alone in AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65. Recommend thymectomy for this 29-year-old regardless of negative CT chest.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Myasthenia gravis, generalized, AChR antibody-positive (MGFA Class IIb), without thymoma; concurrent post-Graves autoimmune thyroid disease

differential.key_features: TRAb negative; no proptosis; no lid retraction; CAS 0; fatigable ptosis and jaw fatigue NOT features of thyroid eye disease; AChR 8.7 nmol/L confirms MG
Normal baseline CMAP; no 50Hz increment; ocular prominent (atypical LEMS); AChR positive
Young woman, no MRI indicated without other brainstem signs; fatigable pattern not seen in structural lesion

optimal_actions.expected_finding: AChR 8.7 nmol/L (markedly elevated — MG confirmed); TRAb negative (thyroid eye disease excluded)
15-24% decremental RNS; positive tensilon test (complete ptosis resolution)
No thymoma; recommend thymectomy per MGTX trial

optimal_actions.action: Initiate pyridostigmine 60mg q4-6h and plan immunosuppression
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Pyridostigmine safe; azathioprine preferred (not mycophenolate — reproductive age)

optimal_actions.action: Refer for thymectomy per MGTX trial evidence even without thymoma
optimal_actions.expected_finding: MGTX trial supports thymectomy benefit in generalized AChR-MG age 18-65 regardless of CT

critical_actions: Exclude thyroid eye disease (TRAb, clinical exam) — prior Graves disease is a red herring
Anti-AChR antibodies clearly positive — MG is the diagnosis
Thymectomy referral per MGTX trial even without thymoma on CT
Avoid mycophenolate in reproductive-age woman — azathioprine preferred
contraindicated_actions: Do NOT attribute ptosis and diplopia to Graves thyroid eye disease without excluding MG
Do NOT use mycophenolate in reproductive-age women (teratogenic)
Do NOT omit thymectomy referral because CT shows no thymoma — MGTX trial
key_reasoning_points: Prior Graves disease is a compelling red herring — TRAb negative and CAS 0 confirms thyroid eye disease is inactive; fatigable ptosis is MG
AChR binding antibody 8.7 nmol/L is clearly in the unambiguous diagnostic range
Masseter RNS (24% decrement) directly explains the jaw fatigue symptom — clinicians should order facial muscle RNS when jaw fatigue is prominent
MGTX trial (NEJM 2016) provides Class I evidence for thymectomy benefit in all generalized AChR-MG patients 18-65 regardless of imaging
Polyautoimmunity (Graves disease + MG) is well-recognized and reflects shared autoimmune predisposition

red_herrings.data_point: Prior Graves disease with history of thyroid eye disease
red_herrings.location: past medical history and ophthalmology referral
red_herrings.intended_effect: Prior Graves disease prompts clinician and ophthalmologist to attribute ptosis and diplopia to thyroid eye disease reactivation, delaying MG diagnosis
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: TRAb negative, no proptosis, no lid retraction — Graves inactive; fatigable ptosis and jaw fatigue are diagnostic of MG, not thyroid eye disease
